releases.body:
# v0.49.61

This patch makes Oh My Pi advisors work with Magic Context again on Oh My Pi 18.20.2 and later.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin and restart Oh My Pi. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Oh My Pi: every advisor turn refused, then the advisor halted (issue 940, thanks @Qiiks for the report):** Magic Context lets an Oh My Pi advisor's own requests through its safety check by recognising OMP's stock advisor prompt. Oh My Pi 18.20.2 removed the block that prompt used to start with, so on 18.20.2 and later no advisor was recognised, stock or customised, and each advisor turn was refused until OMP stopped the advisor. Magic Context now recognises the stock advisor prompt with or without that block. Your own `instructions:` in `WATCHDOG.yml` still work, because Oh My Pi adds them after the stock prompt. An advisor request after Oh My Pi compacts the advisor's own context is now recognised too; before, it was refused on every version. Main-session requests are checked exactly as before: a prompt you type that starts like an advisor update is still not treated as one.

# v0.49.60

This patch fixes Pi sessions that could stop shrinking after Pi's own compaction or a failed reply, makes Magic Context take over when Pi reports a context overflow, counts images at their token cost instead of their size in bytes, and fixes Oh My Pi's `antigravity-cli` provider re-compacting after every compaction.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin and restart the host. No database migration is needed.

A Pi or Oh My Pi session whose newest history summary ends partway through a turn rebuilds its request once after the update. That turn's prompt comes back, so the model sees the prompt it is answering. Sessions whose summary ends at the end of a turn send exactly the same requests as before.

## Fixed

- **Pi: a session stopped shrinking and kept sending its summarized history (issue 938, thanks @expiren for the detailed report and the session details):** Magic Context removes the messages a history summary covers by finding the summary's last message in the request. When Pi hides that message (a failed reply it retries), Magic Context places the cut by position in the session instead. That fallback gave up whenever the request also held Pi's own compaction summary, so every summarized message, images included, stayed in the request on every turn. The fallback now cuts exactly as the normal path does, and logs when a cut cannot be placed instead of silently cutting nothing. It never removes the prompt of the turn the summary ends in, so the model never answers a prompt it can't see.
- **Pi: a request could go out without the history summary:** if inserting the summary failed, the turn went out with neither the summary nor the cut. Magic Context now replays the last good request, or refuses the turn when there is none.
- **Pi: overflows that Pi detected left Magic Context's recovery off (issue 938):** Pi recognises some provider errors as context overflows that Magic Context's own patterns missed. Magic Context now also asks the running host's overflow check, and it arms its overflow recovery when Pi is about to retry a request that failed for an overflow. A reply that succeeded but reported more input than Pi's configured window arms nothing, because the provider accepted it.
- **Pi: images counted at their size in bytes (issue 938):** a base64 image counted as tens of thousands of tokens in Magic Context's size checks, and images in tool outputs counted as fixed, so the emergency drop could not remove them. Images now count at a fixed token cost per image, can be dropped with the tool output that carries them, and no longer block replaying the last good request.
- **Oh My Pi, `antigravity-cli`: compacting again right after a compaction (issue 939, thanks @DeemoASCII):** this provider reports each tool-call step with only `usage.contextTokens`. Magic Context ignored that field, so after a compaction it kept reading the old peak and compacted again. It now uses `contextTokens` when the other usage counters are all zero; other providers are unchanged. `antigravity-cli` also gets the same window as `google-antigravity`, whose output is not reserved out of the input window.

# v0.49.59

This patch makes history summaries and the dreamer work again on OpenCode 2.3 with the Superpowers plugin, makes the dreamer work on OpenCode 2.3's Claude Agent provider, lets a manual `/ctx-dream` use dreamer settings changed while the host runs, keeps tags and `ctx_reduce` reminders out of Pi and Oh My Pi sessions that cannot call `ctx_reduce`, moves the historian's debug files out of your project, and stops Oh My Pi WebSocket continuations from being refused over a field the provider never receives.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin and restart the host. OpenCode 2 does not update npm plugins by itself, so update it as the docs describe. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode 2.3 with Superpowers: history summaries and dreamer tasks refused (issue 937, thanks @elvisw for the report and the isolated host runs):** since 0.49.56, Magic Context's hidden summary and dreamer runs are created without a parent session, so they no longer wake your session (issue 913). Superpowers adds its bootstrap text to the first message of any session without a parent, so it now added it to these runs too. Magic Context's safety check read only the first text part, missed the run's own registered prompt behind the bootstrap, and refused the run with `hidden_prompt_unrecognized`. The check now finds the registered prompt in any text part of the message, and still refuses a message that doesn't carry one. The message is then replaced with the run's registered prompt as before, so text another plugin added never reaches the hidden model. Runs on setups without such a plugin send exactly the same requests as before.
- **OpenCode 2.3, Claude Agent provider: dreamer tasks invented their own output format and committed nothing (issue 935, thanks @mgt-l for the report and the kept child sessions):** OpenCode 2.3's `claude-agent` provider builds the system prompt from Claude Code's own prompt and drops the request's first system part. Magic Context's hidden runs put each task's instructions, including its output format, in exactly that part, so the model never saw them. On that provider the task's instructions now go at the start of the run's first message, identical on every step of the run so the provider's prompt cache holds. This covers the dreamer tasks and the historian. Requests to every other provider are unchanged, byte for byte.
- **OpenCode 2: a manual `/ctx-dream` ignored dreamer settings changed after startup (issue 936, thanks @mgt-l):** the configuration reference marks the dreamer's model, variant and fallback models as live, and scheduled runs already followed changes. A manual `/ctx-dream` used the settings the plugin started with. It now reads the live configuration too. On OpenCode 1, a manual `/ctx-dream` also honours a dreamer turned off after startup.
- **Pi and Oh My Pi: sessions that cannot call `ctx_reduce` got tags and reduce reminders (issue 904, thanks @TheOrdinaryWow):** Magic Context added `§N§` tags, `ctx_reduce` guidance and both reduce reminders to sessions whose tool list has no `ctx_reduce`, such as an Oh My Pi task child spawned from plan mode. Now all three appear only while the session's next request can call the tool, checked on every request. When another extension removes the tool or puts it back, the session rebuilds its prompt once, at that request, and tags that come back keep their numbers. Oh My Pi task children are now treated as subagents, as on OpenCode: no history summaries and no note reminders. A forked session that inherited history from its source keeps it.
- **Historian debug files were written into your project (issue 934, thanks @zapadinsky):** when a historian pass fails its checks, Magic Context keeps the model's response for debugging. These files went to `.cortexkit/magic-context/historian/` inside the project. They now go to the operating system's temporary directory, per session, next to Magic Context's log: `<temp dir>/<host>/magic-context/historian/<session id>

# v0.49.57

This patch stops Oh My Pi subagents from being cut off on their first turns, says clearly why a turn was refused when history summaries keep failing, clears stale context limits after a model or route change, and stops the memory mural from showing boxes for memories in non-Latin scripts.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin and restart the host. OpenCode 2 does not update npm plugins by itself, so update it as the docs describe. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Oh My Pi: task subagents refused and ended within seconds (issue 931, thanks @DeemoASCII for the report and the root-cause work):** Magic Context checks that the request Oh My Pi sends matches the turn it prepared. On Oh My Pi 18.19 and 18.20, three request shapes failed that check, and the refusal ended the subagent:
  - **Parallel tool calls stored in a different order.** When a reply's parallel tool calls finished out of order, Oh My Pi replayed them in their finishing order, not their order in the message. This is what ended the reporter's subagents.
  - **Repeated tool-call ids.** Some providers reuse a tool-call id, in one reply or across replies. Oh My Pi renames the repeat, but its replay still sends the original ids, adds the renamed call, and gives an unanswered call a placeholder result. Both full requests and chained continuations are covered.
  - **The `# Juice` reasoning item.** When Oh My Pi turns reasoning off for some OpenAI models, it adds a short instruction item at the end of the request. It is now recognized exactly.

  Any other difference is still refused. Oh My Pi's automatic Auto-learn capture turns stay off under Magic Context, because they resend the raw, unmanaged conversation. They are now refused quietly, without refusal entries in your session.
- **A refused turn blamed the wrong summary failure (issue 930, thanks @mcheiyue):** when context reaches 95% and a history summary does not finish in time, the turn is refused, as before. The message used to quote whatever summary error was stored last, often from an earlier run. It now names the summary run it waited for and its state, how many summary runs have failed in a row and since when, how full the context is, and what to do: check `/ctx-status`, change the history model or its fallbacks, or run `/ctx-recomp`. Errors are shown with paths and secret-shaped values removed. After 3 failed summary runs in a row, a notice now tells you so before the session reaches 95%. It repeats only if the failures continue. This works the same on OpenCode and Pi.
- **A stale context limit stayed after a model or route change (issues 928 and 929, thanks @mcheiyue):** when a provider refuses a request for its length, Magic Context records that model's limit. On OpenCode 2 and Pi, a later, larger request that the provider accepted did not clear the limit. On OpenCode, switching away from a model whose last request was refused did not clear it either, so it came back when you switched back. Now an accepted request above the limit clears it on every host, and leaving the model that owns a limit clears it. On Pi, the turn that switches models no longer applies the previous model's limit. A limit is never cleared by a request that fits under it, because that proves nothing. If a gateway serves one model name through routes with different limits, switching to another model for one turn and back clears a stale limit.
- **The memory mural drew boxes for memories in non-Latin scripts (issue 932, thanks @G0-0000):** the mural's font has no glyphs for Chinese and many other scripts, so those memories drew as rows of identical boxes, and the image was still sent and counted. The mural now leaves out any memory it cannot draw, and sends no image when it can draw none. Accented letters and typographic quotes and dashes are drawn as their plain forms. Murals that drew correctly before are unchanged.

# v0.49.56

This patch stops summaries and background memory work from waking your session on OpenCode 2.3, and lets very large Pi and Oh My Pi sessions take turns again.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin and restart the host. OpenCode 2 does not update npm plugins by itself, so update it as the docs describe. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode 2.3: summaries and memory upkeep woke your session (issue 913, thanks @HenrijsS for the report and @Neko-Yukari for the fix):** Magic Context writes summaries and runs its memory upkeep in hidden helper sessions. It created each one as a child of your session, and OpenCode 2.3 reports every finished child to its parent and starts a new turn there. So each summary and each upkeep run showed up as a message in your session, and your agent answered it. Hidden runs are now separate sessions with no parent. They are removed when they end. If a run is cut off by a crash or restart, a cleanup pass removes it later, at startup and every 30 minutes, once its own time limit has passed. Cleanup never removes a run that is still going. Checked on OpenCode 2.3.0 and on 2.0.22.
- **Pi and Oh My Pi: every turn refused on very large sessions (issue 920, thanks @snoproblem):** on a session with many thousands of tool calls, a one-time repair of duplicate tag numbers ran as one large step. It took longer than the turn's time limit, was undone, and started over on the next turn, so every turn was refused after about 35 seconds. The repair now saves its progress in small steps that each fit the limit, so a large session catches up over a few turns and stays fast after that. On a test session the size of the report, the first turn takes about 5 seconds and later turns about 25 milliseconds.
